text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Increased 5xx rate and host reboots observed for inference-pool-prod in us-west-2. Alert threshold crossed at 09:14 UTC.

alex: acked. I'm oncall. hitting #oncall-handoff in 2.

maria: I see a spike in API errors and a few pods in CrashLoopBackOff, + timeout on GPU-backed nodes. Customers affected: real-time chat (prod orgs) — p95 latency + errors.

alex: timeline?

maria: quick timeline from metrics:
- 09:13 UTC: rolling increase in GPU host host-uk2-07 IOPS and kernel errors
- 09:14 UTC: provider reported host reboot for host-uk2-07
- 09:15 UTC: node agent restarted, kubelet re-registered, several inference pods failed to recover due to NVML errors
- 09:17 UTC: incident-bot alert for >3% 5xx on inference-api route
- 09:22 UTC: we started draining host-uk2-07; still seeing 500s during reschedule

sre-jordan: paste logs (dmesg, nvml) pls. Also CPU/GPU error counters.

maria: attaching snippets:
```
[  451.123456] EDAC MC0: CPU0: CE page 0x1a2b3c: 0x00000004
[  451.123789] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error
[  452.456000] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0x23:123)
[  453.000111] nvlddmkm: GPU has fallen off the bus. GPU recovery required.
```

maria: NVML query returned ECC errors increasing on GPU0 and GPU2 prior to reboot.

eng-runtime-lead: can you also paste the inference runtime logs for the failing pods? we need to see whether KV cache restore failed or if the runtime panicked.

maria: runtime logs:
```
2025-05-04T09:12:58Z ERROR runtime/serve.go:234 kvcache: failed to mmap cache shard: invalid argument
2025-05-04T09:13:05Z WARN  runtime/driver.go:178 nvml: ECC corrected errors incremented: gpu0=12 gpu1=0 gpu2=9
2025-05-04T09:13:40Z ERROR runtime/serve.go:299 driver: gpu lost, draining request queue
```

alex: immediate mitigations?

sre-jordan: actions in progress: 1) cordon + drain host-uk2-07 2) reschedule affected pods to cpu-backup-pool (non-GPU) or to spare GPU nodes in us-west-2-denser-pool 3) increase burst capacity (scale group) 4) open ticket with cloud provider for host hardware trace.

ops-bot: Command succeeded: `kubectl drain host-uk2-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (started at 09:22:14 UTC).

cloud-support: opened provider ticket TKT-992114. Provider prelim reply: host-uk2-07 experienced a hypervisor-level evacuation and a kernel panic, with ECC corrected error counts prior to forced reboot. They requested the host-system logs (we provided dmesg + nvml).

alex: customer impact status? which orgs hit errors and what's the mitigation path?

maria: affected customers: 4 orgs with real-time features (IDs redacted). For most, requests fell back to retries; however streaming sessions saw abrupt disconnects. Estimated ~2-5% of total prod requests during the window.

eng-runtime-lead: temporary mitigation: enable fallback routing to hosted-cpu-fallback for sessions older than 60s and allow partial results. Can we flip that?

alex: do it. Maria, coordinate with traffic-engineering to add route rule. Notify customers via status page.

maria: routing change applied at 09:28 UTC: `route add inference:gpu => inference:cpu-fallback when latency>2s or retry>=1`

sre-jordan: hypothesis tracking:
- H1: Noisy neighbor caused PCIe AER + ECC corrected errors -> GPU driver degraded -> kernel/hypervisor panicked -> host reboot. (evidence: AER logs, ECC counts)
- H2: GPU hardware fault independent of neighbor (evidence: recurring ECC on same GPU IDs, nvml RmInitAdapter failed)
- H3: driver/firmware regression triggered by specific model/sequence length leading to memory corruption (evidence: mmap errors in runtime).

alex: assign H1 to cloud-support to validate host-level telemetry and migration logs. Assign H2 to provider ticket (TKT-992114) — ask for GPU replacement and vendor ECC hist. Assign H3 to eng-runtime for further repro.

cloud-support: provider returned preliminary logs: repeated corrected ECC errors on pci@0000:65:00.0, then AER uplink stall, then hypervisor-initiated reboot due to watchdog. They noted that this host had noisy neighbor VM with high PCIe traffic in previous 6 hours. Provider suggests hardware swap and hypervisor patch.

maria: after draining, error rate dropped to baseline by ~09:36 UTC. We resumed normal routing at 09:40 UTC after verifying replacements and rebalancing.

ops-bot: autoscaler: added 3 nodes to us-west-2-denser-pool at 09:25 UTC (scaling event id: scale-8372).

eng-runtime-lead: repro tasks: capture a pod-level repro with high-throughput microbench + ECC stress. I'll schedule a canary in staging with stress pattern.

alex: handoff note for next oncall (maria taking next):
- current status: host-uk2-07 drained and marked unschedulable, pods moved, error rate normalized. provider ticket open TKT-992114.
- action items for next oncall: follow up provider RCA, collect pre/post ECC counters for replaced host, verify firmware/driver OSS versions, and complete postmortem.

maria: ack. I'm taking the oncall. I'll own postmortem draft. Adding checklist: logs to attach: `/var/log/dmesg/host-uk2-07.log`, `/var/log/nvml/nvml-host-uk2-07.log`, runtime logs from failing pods (attached), and cloud provider hypervisor trace.

sre-jordan: quick note — we should add automated alert that correlates AER/ECC counters rising with host reboot probability and trigger proactive cordon when threshold exceeded. Filing infra ticket INFRA-546.

cloud-support: provider updated TKT-992114: they are provisioning replacement host and will permanently isolate that rack's noisy tenant. They will also share ECC stats and hypervisor kernel panic stack. ETA for full hardware swap 48-72h.

alex: thanks team. moving this thread to postmortem workstream. tagging #postmortems and setting owner to maria. Closing oncall chat at 09:42 UTC.

maria: postmortem plan: timeline, impact, hypothesis, evidence, mitigations, followups (provider swap, infra alert, runtime hardening). I'll post draft in #postmortems in 24h.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: Error rate returned to baseline and affected nodes drained. Root owner assigned: maria.
